content:
elaine: Heads up 1 - Our new partner SummitStack sent a full compliance dump for marketplace onboarding: firmware images, manifest.json (with serials), detailed pen-report, SOC2 excerpt, and supplier questionnaire. Legal/security want a reproducible publish/playbook so we don't hand-edit artifacts.
rod: Can we standardize the split: PUBLIC (redacted metadata + soc excerpt), RESTRICTED (presign to NDA reviewers), ARCHIVE (raw evidence with CMK + retention)?
ojas-partner: SummitStack prefers minimal public disclosure. They'll sign an attestation. They also asked what exact fields we consider "unique identifiers" so they can redact upstream.
mia-legal: Legal asks: 1) Publish only a manifest with unique identifiers removed or replaced with deterministic placeholders; 2) include a one-line attestation from SummitStack; 3) add a short APH clause in the listing copy stating that full artifacts are available to authorized reviewers under NDA. Pen report and firmware remain restricted.
ashley-sec: Security requirements: - Redact fields: serial, hw_id, mac, device_key, internal_hostname - Use deterministic placeholders so cross-artifact correlation is possible (e.g., REDACTED-<8hex>) - Record SHA256 of raw and redacted artifacts in audit log - Presign links TTL = 7 days default; require access ticket + approver - Store originals in KMS-encrypted bucket with MFA delete and 12 month retention.
rod: Dev ops note: we'll automate redaction + placeholder mapping via a small lambda. Suggest deterministic placeholder = "REDACTED-" + sha256(fieldvalue)[:8]. Example python snippet to include in runbook.
elaine: can someone post a tiny jq/sed/jinja example for partners so they can pre-redact before upload? keep it minimal.
rod: jq example to zero out fields and remove cert blobs: ```bash
jq '.serial = "REDACTED" | .hw_id = "REDACTED" | .device_key = "REDACTED" | del(.signer_cert)' manifest.json > manifest.public.json
```
nashley-sec: deterministic placeholder example for runbook: ```python
import hashlib

def redact(v):
  return 'REDACTED-'+hashlib.sha256(v.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
```
ops-bot: ops-bot created ticket MP-2219 to implement presign gating + audit capture: https://confluence.redwood.internal/marketplace/summitstack-playbook :ticket:
mia-legal: Listing copy suggested line: "Sensitive device identifiers and internal configuration details have been removed from the public package; full artifacts are available to authorized reviewers under NDA." I'll finalize the exact wording.
ojas-partner: SummitStack asked: do you need the full cert chain for verification? we can provide signer_cert to reviewers only.
ashley-sec: Yes provide signer_cert only to NDA'd reviewers via presign. Public package must not contain PEM blobs. Also require partner to include contact for vulnerability witness window and confirmation that keys were not exfiltrated.
rod: Operational checklist I'll own: 1) validate partner uploaded expected files 2) run deterministic redaction lambda (store mapping in ephemeral key-value store) 3) compute SHA256 of raw and redacted bundles 4) push public bundle to marketplace assets 5) upload raw evidence to secure bucket with CMK and MFA delete 6) create presign link only after access ticket approved 7) write audit entry with requester, approver, purpose, hashes.
elaine: timeline: Rod to implement redaction lambda + runbook by Thu, Mia to finalize legal wording today, Ashley to prepare security checklist, Ojas to get attestation and reviewer contacts by Wed.
ops-bot: ops-bot recommended IAM pattern: ephemeral reviewer role with s3:GetObject on specific prefix plus condition aws:RequestTag/requesterTicketId ; CloudTrail events to be aggregated into audit S3 prefix.
mia-legal: Also require SummitStack sign an evidence access addendum (one-page) appended to NDA. I'll draft and send.
ojas-partner: I'll coordinate NDA and the witness window for pen-test. also will get a stripped SOC2 excerpt focused on controls for change management and key custody.
rod: I'll share the redaction lambda stub and a short runbook we can attach to partner onboarding docs.
ashley-sec: After dry-run we should run a verification: confirm redacted manifest doesn't leak identifiers (simple grep), verify placeholder determinism across artifacts, and check audit log contains raw hash.
elaine: Great. Marking this thread canonical for SummitStack marketplace evidence flow. Please post presign links, SHA256s, and runbook links in this thread when ready. Ping @elaine if anything slips.
